title: The learner switcher names Enter, a key the Fire TV remote does not have
body:
## Summary
The learner switcher's caption said "Enter goes back to the desk" / "Enter to sit at this desk" (desk/src/tv/screens.tsx:471); the remote has Select, and every other shell caption names Select.

## Description
Learner draws the caption from the focused card. It was the only shell caption naming a keyboard key; the others say "Select: go to the desk" (desk/src/tv/screens.tsx:51), "Select to skip the break" (:317), "Select for a hint" (:149). The stick deadline walk of 2026-10-21 (row 10) read "the line says what Enter and Menu do" on the device. Fixed: Select.

## Flow
- TV: Down to Someone else, Select -> the learner cards
- Caption under a card: "... Enter to sit at this desk" -> a remote with no Enter key
- Fix: the two strings say Select; a server-render test holds every stop

## Expected impact
The learner at the sofa reads the button they have. Could break: nothing; copy only.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the caption names the remote's own button
Before: 1 shell caption names a keyboard key; the new Learner render test failed at focus 0
After: 0; Learner rendered at all three stops names Select (tools/tv-keys-test.cjs green)
Method: gate - server-render of Learner (red then green)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: desk/src/tv/screens.tsx:471 (was "Enter goes back to the desk" / "Enter to sit at this desk"); desk/src/tv/screens.tsx:51,149,317 name Select; docs/concepts/STICK-DEADLINE-WALK-2026-10-21.md row 10

title: Three On Air rules sit at 24 px, off the type scale the reference page was already moved off
body:
## Summary
.chan, .card .k and .card .m in desk/src/design/on-air.css were 24 px, between the 20-22 px labels and the 26-30 px small figures of docs/DESIGN-ON-AIR.md.

## Description
docs/DESIGN-ON-AIR.md:70-82 sets labels 20-22 px and small figures 26-30, nothing else under 28. The prototype reference fixed its two 24 px sites in 0609f68c (prototype/identity/on-air.src.html:55,65); the desk's own sheet kept the same rules at 24 px (desk/src/design/on-air.css:51,92,97): the page counter, "Select to skip the break", the head-to-head time words, the learner card kicker and "at the desk now". A pair where only one side was fixed. Fixed: 26 px, held by a scan of every size in the sheet.

## Flow
- Scan every font-size / font shorthand in on-air.css, comments stripped
- Before: 3 rules at 24 px
- Fix 24 -> 26; the scan is a test in tools/tv-recap-test.cjs

## Expected impact
The TV obeys its own type scale; the learner cards, break screen, page counter and WritingTV cards grow 2 px in those lines. Could break: a 2 px reflow; a TV capture is owed.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every On Air size on the documented scale
Before: 3 rules off the scale (24 px)
After: 0 (tv-recap-test green; a seeded 24 px rule is found)
Method: gate - CSS scan test, red then green
Result: better
Gate: none

title: A stream reopen scheduled before the page went opened a stream nobody owned
body:
## Summary
useSession's onerror schedules open() after a back-off; open() never read the cleanup's `dead` flag, so a timer pending at unmount opened an EventSource with no owner (desk/src/tv/useSession.ts:32).

## Description
Registry: realtime-events / subscription-lifecycle ("the cancelled flag: teardown races the handshake" - the continuation must check the flag). reopen() checked `dead`; the timer path did not. Both surfaces use the hook; from a phone the zombie stream keeps that device counted in phonesLive (desk/src/lib/session/streams.ts:14). Fixed: open() returns when dead.

## Flow
- Stream errors -> setTimeout(open, reopenDelay)
- Page unmounts (navigation, Fast Refresh) -> cleanup closes the current stream
- Timer fires -> before: a new EventSource nobody closes; after: nothing

## Expected impact
No orphan stream after a page goes; a phone that left is not counted as here. Could break: nothing while mounted (asserted: a mounted page still reopens).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - no stream outlives its owner
Before: 1 stream open after unmount (test red)
After: 0; mounted reopen still 2 streams, the new one open
Method: gate - useSession run outside React with a fake EventSource and timer queue
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: desk/src/tv/useSession.ts:32 onerror -> setTimeout(open, ...); :34 reopen checks dead; :28 the new guard; desk/src/lib/session/streams.ts:14 presence counts devices with a stream

title: No test held every store screen to a draw on the TV; a dropped case went blank
body:
## Summary
desk/src/app/tv/page.tsx:201-217 ScreenFor falls to `default: return null` for any screen no owner or case draws; no suite read its cases.

## Description
Who draws a screen is split between the module owners (landing, essayOwns, mathsOwns, paperOwns, lingaOwns) and ScreenFor's 13 cases (§4.7 hand-maintained list). A new Screen (41 today) or a dropped case is a blank stage - the failure the 2026-10-13 sweep fixed by hand for hint and lesson. Built: a test derived from the store's Screen union over every subject.

## Flow
- Read the Screen union from desk/src/lib/session/store.ts
- For each screen x subject: owned, or a ScreenFor case (comments stripped)
- Seed: the page without case "break" -> three gaps reported

## Expected impact
A screen added to the store without a TV draw fails the desk gate instead of reaching the TV blank. Could break: nothing (test only).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every screen is drawn
Before: 0 tests derive draw coverage; a page without case "break" passes every suite
After: 1 derived test over 123 screen x subject pairs: 0 gaps; the seeded page reports break/maths, break/english, break/essay
Method: gate - derived test with a seeded control
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: desk/src/app/tv/page.tsx:172 owners, :201-217 ScreenFor, :217 default: return null; grep of tools/*.cjs for ScreenFor before: no reader

title: Reduced motion left the page band and the recap tiles moving
body:
## Summary
On Air's prefers-reduced-motion block cut .btn and .read .img but not .read .focus-band or .rc .rc-tile (desk/src/design/on-air.css:106,124,135).

## Description
Registry: motion; .ai/registry-map.json records the tv-surface x motion deviation at the page marker. On Air "motion: cuts, not fades". Four rules transition; two were left under the preference. Fixed: all four, held by a test that reads the transitioned selectors from the sheet.

## Flow
- Set prefers-reduced-motion
- Down on a page: the focus band slides (.18 s); Left/Right on the recap: the tile lifts (.25 s)
- Fix: both named in the block; the test derives the list

## Expected impact
A learner who asked for less motion gets cuts everywhere On Air moves. Could break: nothing without the preference.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the preference is honoured on every transition
Before: 2 of 4 transitions not cut (test red)
After: 0 of 4
Method: gate - derived CSS test, red then green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: desk/src/design/on-air.css:124 (was `.btn, .read .img`); :106 .read .focus-band transition top/height; :135-136 .rc .rc-tile transition transform; .ai/registry-map.json tv-surface motion deviation

title: Every lower-third blurs its backdrop, an offscreen GPU pass on the stick
body:
## Summary
.lt .txt carries backdrop-filter: blur(6px) (desk/src/design/on-air.css:56) on the page, hint, sentence and pair screens; on the stick a backdrop filter is an offscreen pass, the cost class that made layer drop-shadows the landing's main cost.

## Description
docs/concepts/STICK-PERFORMANCE-2026-10-20.md ranked composited blur passes first (8.7 -> 55 fps when removed on the landing). The lower-third is the On Air "charcoal-glass" block. A desktop Chromium probe (the real on-air.css, a hint-like stage, 1920x1080) shows the blur is visible only where the lower-third sits over the band: 31,997 of 2,073,600 px differ, max channel delta 124, PSNR 42.3 dB. So removing it is not free on the look, and its cost on the stick is unmeasured.

## Flow
- Measure the stick's idle and Select windows on hint and sentence with the blur on and off
- If the cost is real, replace the blur by a flat rgba(20,22,26,.85) where the band sits under it
- Capture both and compare

## Expected impact
Possibly smoother hint and sentence screens on the stick. Could break: the glass look over the band.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - fewer offscreen passes on the stick
Before: unmeasured on the stick; look delta 1.5% of pixels, PSNR 42.3 dB (desktop probe)
After: predicted: one fewer offscreen pass per lower-third
Method: simulation - the stick is the operator's device and no dev server runs here; the look half was probed
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence: desk/src/design/on-air.css:56 `.lt .txt { ... backdrop-filter: blur(6px) ... }`; drawn at desk/src/tv/screens.tsx:69,143,176,263; probe: 31997/2073600 px differ, max delta 124, PSNR 42.28 dB
instrument: tools/stick-perf/perf.mjs + window.mjs on the hint and sentence screens, with and without `.lt .txt { backdrop-filter: none }` laid over by DevTools; plus the look probe (PSNR) on the same screens

title: Back from a module rebuilds the whole landing
body:
## Summary
desk/src/app/tv/page.tsx:172 renders LandingTV only while s.screen is landing, so every Back unmounts the module and mounts the landing again; the stick perf pass left it open (about 150 ms main-thread mount plus the live layers' raster).

## Description
docs/concepts/STICK-PERFORMANCE-2026-10-21.md "Left open": "Back rebuilds the landing. Keeping it mounted under the modules would save the main-thread mount (about 150 ms). The raster remains." and pass 3: "Keeping the landing mounted under the modules would need Paper.tsx or app/tv/page.tsx, which this pass did not own." This round owns app/tv/page.tsx; the change is a structural one with memory cost (the stills stay resident, +46 MB GL measured in pass 3).

## Flow
- Keep LandingTV mounted, hidden (visibility or content-visibility) while a module is up
- Measure Back windows and GL mtrack on the stick
- Keep only if Back improves and memory stays in budget

## Expected impact
A faster Back on the stick. Could break: memory headroom inside modules; focus and key routing while hidden.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - Back reaches the landing without a remount
Before: about 150 ms main-thread mount per Back (STICK-PERFORMANCE-2026-10-21.md)
After: predicted: the mount gone, the raster kept
Method: simulation - a stick measurement; no device or dev server in this round
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: tools/stick-perf scenarios: Back from each module, the 1.2 s window's longest gap and frames, with the landing kept mounted (hidden) under the modules vs today

title: A paired phone with its page closed reads as "No phone is connected" in three captions
body:
## Summary
desk/src/tv/keys.ts:278, desk/src/tv/mathsRows.ts:406 and desk/src/tv/writingScreen.ts:62 say "No phone is connected" whenever phonesLive is 0, while the same screens show the phone as joined; the walk found it three times (F3, M3, W1).

## Description
phonesLive counts phones with an open stream (desk/src/lib/session/streams.ts:14); `joined` means a phone is listed. A real phone with its screen off drops its stream and reads as "not connected" beside a "Phone joined" badge (docs/concepts/STICK-DEADLINE-WALK-2026-10-21.md F3, M3, W1). One rule in three files, two of them outside this round (maths, writing contexts). Fix: when joined and not live, say the phone's page is closed ("Open the desk on your phone. Back cancels.").

## Flow
- Pair a phone, lock it
- Open an essay, maths or writing hand-off on the TV
- Caption says "No phone is connected" beside "Phone joined"

## Expected impact
The learner is told to wake the phone, not to pair again. Could break: tests that pin the three strings.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - one meaning of connected on one screen
Before: 3 captions contradict the joined badge (walk F3, M3, W1)
After: predicted 0
Method: simulation - walked on the device by the 10-21 walk; the fix spans two contexts this round does not own
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: desk/src/tv/keys.ts:278; desk/src/tv/mathsRows.ts:406; desk/src/tv/writingScreen.ts:62; desk/src/lib/session/streams.ts:14; docs/concepts/STICK-DEADLINE-WALK-2026-10-21.md F3, M3, W1
instrument: a server-render test of the three hand-off captions with joined:true, phonesLive:0 (and the badge beside them), asserting one meaning of "connected"

title: The lesson player is told Play and Pause with targetOrigin "*"
body:
## Summary
desk/src/tv/screens.tsx:206,224 and desk/src/maths/MathsTV.tsx:1122,1133 post the YouTube command to the embed with "*", not to https://www.youtube-nocookie.com.

## Description
The embed is always youtube-nocookie (screens.tsx:216). "*" delivers the message to whatever the frame has navigated to. The payload is only a play/pause command, so the exposure is small, but the fix is one constant beside playerCommand (desk/src/tv/keys.ts:218). Half the sites are in the maths context; fixing only this round's two would leave the pair split, so it goes whole to a worker that owns both.

## Flow
- Export PLAYER_ORIGIN from tv/keys.ts
- Use it at the four postMessage sites
- A scan test forbids "*" there

## Expected impact
Commands reach only the player. Could break: a lesson embed served from another YouTube host would stop obeying Play/Pause.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - messages addressed to their one origin
Before: 4 postMessage sites with "*"
After: predicted 0
Method: simulation - two of the four sites are outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
instrument: a source scan of desk/src for postMessage(..., "*"): 4 sites today, 0 after; plus playerCommand's origin constant exported from tv/keys.ts

title: A step's calls still fire when the desk refused its events
body:
## Summary
runStep (desk/src/tv/keys.ts:788-798) cancels the calls only when a post throws; a post that answers non-ok resolves, so a refused topic.open still fires /api/practice.

## Description
The doc comment says "Events that fail to post cancel the calls and apply every onFail". useSession's post returns the Response and never throws on a status (desk/src/tv/useSession.ts:38), so only a network error reaches the catch at :791. A 5xx or a 400 from badPost (desk/src/app/api/session/route.ts:83) leaves the step going. But a 409 on an ask.cancel the phone already closed (route.ts:85) is benign and must not stop a walk Left/Right, so the rule needs a per-status decision: M, risk 4.

## Flow
- Select on a topic -> topic.open answered 500 (a write that failed)
- runStep fires /api/practice anyway
- Decide: 5xx and 400 cancel the calls; a 409 on ask.cancel does not

## Expected impact
No model call on a desk that refused the event before it. Could break: steps whose first event is an ask.cancel race.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a refused event stops what depended on it
Before: 0 of the non-ok statuses stop the calls (read from runStep)
After: predicted: 5xx and 400 stop them, 409 on a cancel does not
Method: simulation - the status policy needs a decision and a test beyond S
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: desk/src/tv/keys.ts:788-798 runStep; :791 catch only; desk/src/tv/useSession.ts:38 post returns the Response; desk/src/app/api/session/route.ts:83,85
instrument: a runStep test with post resolving {ok:false,status:500} (calls must not fire, onFail applied) and {ok:false,status:409} on an ask.cancel (the walk must still go on)

title: The shell's keymap holds sixteen handlers for screens the modules draw themselves
body:
## Summary
desk/src/tv/keys.ts KEYMAP (:369-763) has 29 handlers; 16 belong to screens Essay Master (6), Math Buddy (9) and Writing (1) draw on their own, and keys.ts imports eight of their row modules.

## Description
The file header says every screen's stop list is read from here so the screen and the key share one list. That holds, but a module's key change now lands in the shell's 798-line file, owned by tv-surface, while the module's own screens live elsewhere (desk/src/essay/EssayTV.tsx, desk/src/maths/MathsTV.tsx). Linga already owns its keys (lingaOwns, LingaTV). A per-module keymap registered with the shell would follow that model. It changes how every module is wired: architecture.

## Flow
- Count KEYMAP handlers by who draws the screen
- Decide: per-module keymaps registered with tvKey (as Linga does), or keep one map
- If split: move handlers with their tests, one module at a time

## Expected impact
A module's key change stays in its module. Could break: the shared helpers (openWaiting, cancelAsk, pairUp) need a home both sides import.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - ownership follows the screen
Before: 29 handlers, 16 for module-drawn screens, 8 row-module imports
After: predicted 13 shell handlers
Method: simulation - a structural change across three contexts
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: architecture
evidence: desk/src/tv/keys.ts:19-25 imports mathsRows, sheetRows, landingRows, writingScreen, recapRows, prepareRows, paperRows, profileRows; :369-763 KEYMAP; :55 lingaOwns

title: The desk build fetches its fonts from Google at build time
body:
## Summary
desk/src/app/layout.tsx:2 loads Barlow and Barlow Condensed through next/font/google, which downloads them during `next build`; a desk rebuilt with no internet does not build.

## Description
At runtime the fonts are self-hosted (the layout's comment), but the build needs fonts.googleapis.com. The stick deadline walk notes the operator's :3000 desk is rebuilt with `next build` for a fix to show. A LAN-only rebuild (a demo venue) would stop there. Vendoring the woff2 files with next/font/local keeps the same CSS variables.

## Flow
- Block the network
- next build -> font download fails (predicted)
- Vendor the faces under desk/src/fonts and use next/font/local

## Expected impact
The desk builds offline. Could break: font metrics if the vendored cut differs.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the build needs no network
Before: predicted: offline build fails at the font fetch
After: predicted: it builds
Method: simulation - no build or network is allowed in this round
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: `next build` with the network blocked (before: fails at the font fetch, predicted), then with next/font/local and the two families vendored
